metadata.label: Former Owner(s)
metadata.value: Wäldä Giyorgis; Lindsay, James Ludovic, 1847-1913

metadata.label: Binding
metadata.value:
Ethiopic binding. Quarter bound in brown/red goat leather with the rest of the wooden boards left exposed. Leather is not adhered directly to the spine, but is secured at head and tail by endband structure and adhered on the boards. Brown leather split braid endbands. Unsupported sewing at 6 stations (three even pairs of sewing stations).

Binding height: 400 mm, width: 344 mm, depth: 51 mm.

metadata.label: Acquisition
metadata.value: Bequeathed by Enriqueta Rylands (1843–1908) in 1908 to The John Rylands Library.

metadata.label: Title
metadata.value: Enoch, Job, and the Book of Kings

metadata.label: Layout
metadata.value:
3 columns, 40 lines per leaf.

Pages have been pricked and scored to assist in writing.

metadata.label: Funding
metadata.value: The John Rylands Research Institute and Library, The University of Manchester

metadata.label: Date of Creation
metadata.value: 18th century

metadata.label: Origin Place
metadata.value: Ethiopia

metadata.label: Collation
metadata.value: 5 bifolios per section. There is evidence of a section having been removed from the centre of the manuscript (between folios 25-26) from a gap in the textblock.

metadata.label: Script
metadata.value: Written in a Ge'ez script, in black and red ink, by a single hand.

metadata.label: Data Source(s)
metadata.value: Description based on Stefan Strelcyn, Catalogue of Ethiopic manuscripts in the John Rylands University Library of Manchester (Manchester University Press, Manchester, 1974), revised and expanded by Jeremy Penner and Jeremy Brown.

metadata.label: Language(s)
metadata.value: Ge'ez

metadata.label: Physical Location
metadata.value: The John Rylands Research Institute and Library

metadata.label: Extent
metadata.value: 67 folios: Leaf height: 395 mm, width: 330 mm.

metadata.label: Additions
metadata.value:
Corrections and marginalia found throughout manuscript.

Pen trials on 1r-1v. The verso contains a note listing the contents of the manuscript.

The work contains a gift of deed on 67r in Ge'ez and Amharic: ኍልቈ ፡ ምድር ፡ ዘድልድል ፡ ዘዓንቀባ ፡ የነገዴ ፡ ፪ምድር ፡ የግራዛ ፡የአባ ፡ ዮሐንስ ።፪ም ፡ የግራዛ ፡ የዘሜና ፡ የዳዊት ።፩ም ፡ የግራዛ ፡ የልብሴ ።፩ም ፡ መቃ ፡ የፊላታዎስ ።፩ም ፡ መቃ ፡ የልጄ ፡ ክሶስ ።፩ም ፡ ማቋ ፡ የዮሐንስ ። ፩ም ፡ መቃ ፡ የተአምሬ ።፩ም ፡ ደንሳ ፡ የፍርዱ ።

metadata.label: Provenance
metadata.value:
Owned by Wäldä Giyorgis.

James Ludovic Lindsay, 26th Earl of Crawford (1847-1913). The inner upper cover bears the armorial bookplate (Ex Libris) identifying the codex as having once been part of the Bibliotheca Lindesiana, the private library of the Lindsay family, Earls of Crawford and Balcarres | Armorial bookplate (Ex Libris): ARMS: Quarterly, 1st and 4th, Gules a fess chequy Argent and Azure; 2nd and 3rd, Or a lion rampant Gules, debruised of a ribbon in bend Sable. CREST: a swan’s head, neck, and wings proper, issuing from an antique ducal coronet Or. SUPPORTERS: two lions, rampant guardant Gules. MOTTO in Latin: Endure fort (Endure bravely) | Bibliotheca Lindesiana | pencilled: 5/G. Pencilled on left inner upper cover: Ethiopic MSS | No 23.

Purchased by Enriqueta Rylands (1843–1908) in 1901 from James Ludovic Lindsay, 26th Earl of Crawford (1847-1913).
